confidence_notes: Six searches in total (one RBA, five price checks). Cappuccino rests on a search-reported Numbeo London figure (about GBP 4.2, Nov 2026), cross-checked with Expatistan (about GBP 4.85, expat area). Beer rests on 2026 UK pint surveys (London about GBP 5.8-6.75), set slightly above the pub average for a restaurant serving. Meal anchors are weaker. Only third-party Numbeo-derived figures surfaced (about USD 20 for an inexpensive meal in 2023, about USD 106 for a mid-range meal for two in 2026), so I adjusted them for inflation. Cocktail (reported GBP 13-17, thin low-sample sources) and wine (no London average found; ONS UK 175 ml about GBP 5.17 in Jan 2025, one London list GBP 7-10) were cross-checked against beer ratios (cocktail about 2.2x, wine about 1.3x). GBP prices were converted to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.35 USD per GBP, which I did not search. Accommodation anchors are holistic general-knowledge estimates for July peak season. No booking pages or listings were checked.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink use London-specific price evidence (no proxy city). Accommodation reflects London's July peak-season market, which sits at the high end of Western European capitals, a similar tier to Paris or Amsterdam. Cocktail and wine were cross-checked against London's beer price relationship.
